apiVersion: miabi.io/v1

  tags: [database, admin, sql, tools]

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: goauthentik
  displayName: authentik
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Self-hosted identity provider — SSO, OAuth2/OIDC, SAML and LDAP — backed by PostgreSQL and Redis.
  category: Security
  icon: https://cdn.simpleicons.org/authentik
  homepage: https://goauthentik.io
  tags: [security, sso, identity, oauth, saml, oidc]
inputs:
  - key: secret_key
    label: Secret key
    help: Signing key for sessions and tokens. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 50
    required: true
  - key: bootstrap_email
    label: Initial admin email
    help: Email for the initial akadmin superuser created on first launch.
    type: string
    required: true
    default: admin@example.com
    pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
  - key: bootstrap_password
    label: Initial admin password
    help: Password for the initial akadmin superuser. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 24
    required: true
databases:
  - name: db
    engine: postgres
    version: "17-alpine"
    placement: auto
  - name: redis
    engine: redis
    version: "8-alpine"
    placement: dedicated
volumes:
  - name: media
# Shared across the server + worker: both processes need the same secret key and
# the same PostgreSQL/Redis connection, so they are declared once here instead of
# being repeated in every application.
stack:
  description: authentik identity provider — a server and a background worker sharing PostgreSQL and Redis.
  env:
    AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY: "{{ .inputs.secret_key }}"
    AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__HOST: "{{ .databases.db.host }}"
    AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__PORT: "{{ .databases.db.port }}"
    AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__USER: "{{ .databases.db.user }}"
    AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__PASSWORD: "{{ .databases.db.password }}"
    AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__NAME: "{{ .databases.db.name }}"
    AUTHENTIK_REDIS__HOST: "{{ .databases.redis.host }}"
    AUTHENTIK_REDIS__PORT: "{{ .databases.redis.port }}"
    AUTHENTIK_REDIS__PASSWORD: "{{ .databases.redis.password }}"
  secretEnv:
    - AUTHENTIK_SECRET_KEY
    - AUTHENTIK_POSTGRESQL__PASSWORD
    - AUTHENTIK_REDIS__PASSWORD
applications:
  - name: server
    primary: true
    image: ghcr.io/goauthentik/server
    tag: "2025.10.2"
    command: ["server"]
    ports:
      - container: 9000
        scheme: http
    env:
      AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.bootstrap_email }}"
      AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.bootstrap_password }}"
    secretEnv:
      - AUTHENTIK_BOOTSTRAP_PASSWORD
    mounts:
      - volume: media
        path: /media
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /-/health/live/
      port: 9000
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 30
  - name: worker
    image: ghcr.io/goauthentik/server
    tag: "2025.10.2"
    command: ["worker"]
    mounts:
      - volume: media
        path: /media

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: ghost
  displayName: Ghost
  version: 1.2.0
  description: Professional publishing platform — a headless Node.js CMS for blogs and newsletters.
  category: CMS
  icon: https://cdn.simpleicons.org/ghost
  homepage: https://ghost.org
  author:
    name: Miabi
    email: community@miabi.io
    website: https://miabi.io
  tags: [blog, cms, publishing, newsletter]
  minMiabi: "0.5.0"

# Questions asked in the install wizard. Referenced below as {{ .inputs.<key> }}.
inputs:
  - key: site_url
    label: Public URL
    help: The full URL your blog will be served on (used for links and webhooks).
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://blog.example.com

# Logical database dependency. placement: auto -> reuse a compatible MySQL
# instance if one exists, else provision a dedicated one; either way Ghost gets
# its own scoped database + user. Tokens resolve identically regardless.
databases:
  - name: db
    engine: mysql
    version: "8.4"
    placement: auto

# Managed volume holding Ghost's content (images, themes, settings).
volumes:
  - name: content

applications:
  - name: ghost
    primary: true
    image: ghost
    tag: "6.45-alpine"
    ports:
      - container: 2368
        scheme: http
    env:
      NODE_ENV: production
      url: "{{ .inputs.site_url }}"
      database__client: mysql
      database__connection__host: "{{ .databases.db.host }}"
      database__connection__port: "{{ .databases.db.port }}"
      database__connection__user: "{{ .databases.db.user }}"
      database__connection__password: "{{ .databases.db.password }}"
      database__connection__database: "{{ .databases.db.name }}"
    secretEnv:
      - database__connection__password
    mounts:
      - volume: content
        path: /var/lib/ghost/content
    resources:
      memory: 512Mi
      cpu: 0.5
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /
      port: 2368
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 20

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: gitlab
  displayName: GitLab
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Complete DevOps platform — Git hosting, merge requests, issues, CI/CD and a package registry.
  category: Development
  icon: https://cdn.simpleicons.org/gitlab
  homepage: https://about.gitlab.com
  tags: [git, vcs, devops, ci-cd, code-review, issues]
inputs:
  - key: external_url
    label: Public URL
    help: The public base URL GitLab is served on. It ends up in clone URLs, emails and every redirect, so set it to the domain you will attach in Miabi.
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://gitlab.example.com
  - key: root_password
    label: Root password
    help: Initial password for the built-in `root` account, applied on first boot only. Leave blank to auto-generate; change it after signing in.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 24
    required: true
  - key: time_zone
    label: Time zone
    help: IANA time zone used for timestamps and scheduled pipelines.
    type: string
    default: UTC
    placeholder: Europe/Brussels

# The omnibus image bundles its own PostgreSQL, Redis, Puma, Sidekiq and Nginx,
# and GitLab supports an external database only with superuser-created extensions
# (pg_trgm, btree_gist) — so this template runs the bundled stack rather than a
# managed Miabi database. Everything stateful lives in the volumes below.
volumes:
  - name: config    # /etc/gitlab      — gitlab.rb, secrets, generated certificates
  - name: logs      # /var/log/gitlab  — per-service logs
  - name: data      # /var/opt/gitlab  — repositories, uploads, the bundled database

applications:
  - name: gitlab
    primary: true
    image: gitlab/gitlab-ce
    tag: "19.2.1-ce.0"
    ports:
      # TLS terminates at Miabi's gateway, so the container only ever speaks HTTP.
      - container: 80
        scheme: http
    env:
      TZ: "{{ .inputs.time_zone }}"
      # Omnibus reads its whole configuration from this variable on every start,
      # which is what keeps the install declarative — nothing to edit by hand
      # inside the container.
      GITLAB_OMNIBUS_CONFIG: |
        external_url '{{ .inputs.external_url }}'
        gitlab_rails['time_zone'] = '{{ .inputs.time_zone }}'
        gitlab_rails['initial_root_password'] = '{{ .inputs.root_password }}'

        # Serve plain HTTP behind the gateway: an https external_url would
        # otherwise make omnibus listen on 443 and try to issue its own
        # certificate, which fails in a container that owns no domain.
        nginx['listen_port'] = 80
        nginx['listen_https'] = false
        letsencrypt['enable'] = false
        nginx['proxy_set_headers'] = {
          'X-Forwarded-Proto' => 'https',
          'X-Forwarded-Ssl' => 'on'
        }

        # SSH is not published by this template (see the README), so point the
        # shell at HTTPS clone URLs rather than advertising an unreachable port.
        gitlab_rails['gitlab_shell_ssh_port'] = 22

        # Right-size the bundled stack for a single node: the default worker
        # counts and the built-in Prometheus suite together cost several GB that
        # a small install has no use for.
        puma['worker_processes'] = 2
        sidekiq['max_concurrency'] = 10
        prometheus_monitoring['enable'] = false
    secretEnv:
      # Carries the initial root password, so it is stored encrypted at rest.
      - GITLAB_OMNIBUS_CONFIG
    mounts:
      - volume: config
        path: /etc/gitlab
      - volume: logs
        path: /var/log/gitlab
      - volume: data
        path: /var/opt/gitlab
    healthcheck:
      # Reconfigure + migrations make the first boot slow (5–10 minutes on a
      # modest node), so the start period is generous — a shorter one would kill
      # the container mid-install.
      type: http
      path: /-/health
      port: 80
      intervalSeconds: 60
      timeoutSeconds: 15
      retries: 5
      startPeriodSeconds: 600

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: invoiceninja
  displayName: Invoice Ninja
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Self-hosted invoicing, quotes, payments and time tracking for freelancers and small businesses.
  category: Productivity
  icon: https://github.com/invoiceninja.png
  homepage: https://invoiceninja.com
  tags: [invoicing, billing, payments, accounting, crm]
inputs:
  - key: app_url
    label: Public URL
    help: The public base URL Invoice Ninja is served on. It ends up in invoice links, payment redirects and emails.
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://invoices.example.com
  - key: admin_email
    label: Admin email
    help: Email of the account created on first start.
    type: string
    required: true
    default: admin@example.com
    pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
  - key: admin_password
    label: Admin password
    help: Password for the initial account. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 24
    required: true
  - key: app_key
    label: Application key
    help: Laravel encryption key. Leave blank to auto-generate — changing it later makes stored credentials unreadable.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 32
    required: true
databases:
  - name: db
    engine: mysql
    version: "8"
    placement: auto
  - name: redis
    engine: redis
    version: "8-alpine"
    placement: dedicated
volumes:
  # public holds the app's web assets, storage its uploads and generated PDFs.
  # Both are shared with the web server, which serves the static files directly.
  - name: public
  - name: storage
applications:
  # The application image is php-fpm only (it exposes 9000 and nothing else), so
  # it is never routed directly — the nginx sidecar below is the entry point.
  - name: app
    image: invoiceninja/invoiceninja-debian
    tag: "5.13.30"
    env:
      APP_URL: "{{ .inputs.app_url }}"
      APP_KEY: "base64:{{ base64 .inputs.app_key }}"
      APP_ENV: production
      APP_DEBUG: "false"
      # TLS terminates at the gateway, which forwards the original scheme and
      # host; requiring HTTPS in the app as well would redirect-loop.
      REQUIRE_HTTPS: "false"
      TRUSTED_PROXIES: "*"

      DB_CONNECTION: mysql
      DB_HOST: "{{ .databases.db.host }}"
      DB_PORT: "{{ .databases.db.port }}"
      DB_DATABASE: "{{ .databases.db.name }}"
      DB_USERNAME: "{{ .databases.db.user }}"
      DB_PASSWORD: "{{ .databases.db.password }}"

      CACHE_DRIVER: redis
      QUEUE_CONNECTION: redis
      SESSION_DRIVER: redis
      REDIS_HOST: "{{ .databases.redis.host }}"
      REDIS_PORT: "{{ .databases.redis.port }}"
      REDIS_PASSWORD: "{{ .databases.redis.password }}"

      # The account seeded on first start; the image skips this once one exists.
      IN_USER_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.admin_email }}"
      IN_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.admin_password }}"

      FILESYSTEM_DISK: debian_docker
      PDF_GENERATOR: snappdf
      PHANTOMJS_PDF_GENERATION: "false"
      MAIL_MAILER: log
    secretEnv:
      - APP_KEY
      - DB_PASSWORD
      - REDIS_PASSWORD
      - IN_PASSWORD
    mounts:
      - volume: public
        path: /var/www/html/public
      - volume: storage
        path: /var/www/html/storage
    healthcheck:
      type: none
  - name: web
    primary: true
    image: nginx
    tag: "1.30-alpine"
    ports:
      - container: 80
        scheme: http
    # The config is carried in env because env is the only interpolated field, and
    # it must name the app's network alias. nginx then waits for the application
    # to publish its assets into the shared volume before serving.
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        printf '%s\n' "$NGINX_CONF" > /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
        until [ -f /var/www/html/public/index.php ]; do sleep 2; done
        exec nginx -g 'daemon off;'
    env:
      NGINX_CONF: |
        client_max_body_size 20M;
        server_tokens off;
        fastcgi_buffers 32 16K;
        gzip on;
        gzip_types text/css application/javascript application/json image/svg+xml;

        server {
            listen 80 default_server;
            server_name _;
            root /var/www/html/public;
            index index.php;
            charset utf-8;

            add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN";
            add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff";

            location / {
                try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$query_string;
            }
            location = /favicon.ico { access_log off; log_not_found off; }
            location = /robots.txt  { access_log off; log_not_found off; }
            error_page 404 /index.php;

            location ~ \.php$ {
                fastcgi_pass {{ .applications.app.alias }}:9000;
                fastcgi_param SCRIPT_FILENAME $realpath_root$fastcgi_script_name;
                include fastcgi_params;
            }
            location ~ /\.(?!well-known).* {
                deny all;
            }
        }
    mounts:
      - volume: public
        path: /var/www/html/public
      - volume: storage
        path: /var/www/html/storage
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /
      port: 80
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 10
      retries: 5
      startPeriodSeconds: 120

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: keycloak
  displayName: Keycloak
  version: 1.0.0
  description: Identity and access management — OpenID Connect, OAuth 2.0 and SAML, with user federation.
  category: Security
  icon: https://cdn.simpleicons.org/keycloak
  homepage: https://www.keycloak.org
  tags: [security, sso, identity, oidc, saml, oauth]
inputs:
  - key: hostname
    label: Public URL
    help: The public base URL Keycloak is served on. It ends up in issuer URLs and every redirect.
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://auth.example.com
  - key: admin_user
    label: Admin username
    help: Temporary admin created on first start; create a permanent account and remove it afterwards.
    type: string
    default: admin
    required: true
  - key: admin_password
    label: Admin password
    help: Password for the bootstrap admin. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 24
    required: true
databases:
  - name: db
    engine: postgres
    version: "17-alpine"
    placement: auto
applications:
  - name: keycloak
    primary: true
    image: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak
    tag: "26.7.1"
    # Production mode; the first boot builds the optimized server image itself.
    command: ["start"]
    ports:
      - container: 8080
        scheme: http
    env:
      KC_DB: postgres
      KC_DB_URL_HOST: "{{ .databases.db.host }}"
      KC_DB_URL_PORT: "{{ .databases.db.port }}"
      KC_DB_URL_DATABASE: "{{ .databases.db.name }}"
      KC_DB_USERNAME: "{{ .databases.db.user }}"
      KC_DB_PASSWORD: "{{ .databases.db.password }}"

      KC_HOSTNAME: "{{ .inputs.hostname }}"

kind: Template
metadata:
  name: posta
  displayName: Posta
  version: 1.1.0
  description: Self-hosted transactional email & SMTP platform — send, receive, and verify email.
  category: Email
  icon: https://github.com/goposta.png
  homepage: https://github.com/goposta/posta
  author:
    name: Jonas Kaninda
    email: me@jkaninda.dev
    website: https://goposta.dev
  tags: [email, smtp, transactional, mail, self-hosted]
  minMiabi: "0.5.0"

inputs:
  - key: web_url
    label: Public URL
    help: The public base URL Posta is served on (used for links, OAuth callbacks, and the API server list).
    type: string
    required: true
    pattern: "^https?://"
    placeholder: https://posta.example.com
  - key: admin_email
    label: Admin email
    help: Email of the initial admin account.
    type: string
    required: true
    default: admin@example.com
    pattern: '^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$'
  - key: admin_password
    label: Admin password
    help: Password for the initial admin account. At least 12 characters — production refuses to seed the first account with a placeholder.
    type: password
    required: true
  - key: jwt_secret
    label: JWT secret
    help: Signing key for auth tokens, tracking links, and the email stamper. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 32
  - key: encryption_key
    label: Encryption key
    help: AES-256-GCM key used to encrypt stored SMTP passwords. Leave blank to auto-generate.
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 32

databases:
  - name: db
    engine: postgres
    version: "17-alpine"
    placement: auto
  - name: redis
    engine: redis
    version: "8-alpine"
    placement: dedicated

# The server and the worker are two processes over one datastore, so everything
# they must agree on lives here and is injected into both containers. An
# app-level variable of the same name wins, which is how each app keeps its own
# role-specific settings below.
stack:
  description: Posta — the API/web server and its dedicated worker, sharing one network and configuration.
  env:
    POSTA_ENV: production

    # Database (a managed PostgreSQL database, resolved by placement). One
    # connection string carries host, port, credentials and database name;
    # POSTA_DB_URL overrides the discrete POSTA_DB_* settings entirely. sslmode is
    # explicit because a URL without it means "prefer", which costs a failed TLS
    # handshake on every connection to a plaintext instance on the private network.
    POSTA_DB_URL: "{{ .databases.db.uri }}?sslmode=disable"

    # Redis (a dedicated managed instance — Miabi sets a password on it). It is
    # the asynq queue both sides speak over: the server enqueues, the worker
    # consumes, so this must be identical on both. POSTA_REDIS_URL likewise
    # overrides the discrete POSTA_REDIS_* settings.
    POSTA_REDIS_URL: "{{ .databases.redis.uri }}"

    # The worker needs both too: it signs outgoing mail with the stamper (JWT
    # secret) and decrypts stored SMTP passwords (encryption key).
    POSTA_JWT_SECRET: "{{ .inputs.jwt_secret }}"
    POSTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY: "{{ .inputs.encryption_key }}"
  secretEnv:
    # Both URLs embed their password, so they are stored encrypted like one.
    - POSTA_DB_URL
    - POSTA_REDIS_URL
    - POSTA_JWT_SECRET
    - POSTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY

applications:
  # The HTTP API and web interface. Keeps the name it had in 1.0.0, so an upgrade
  # from that version maps onto the existing app instead of reading as one app
  # removed and another added.
  - name: posta
    primary: true
    image: jkaninda/posta
    tag: "0.13.1"
    ports:
      - container: 9000
        scheme: http
    env:
      POSTA_WEB_URL: "{{ .inputs.web_url }}"
      POSTA_ADMIN_EMAIL: "{{ .inputs.admin_email }}"
      POSTA_ADMIN_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.admin_password }}"

      # Background jobs belong to the worker below; running them in-process too
      # would double every delivery attempt.
      POSTA_EMBEDDED_WORKER: "false"

      # Email verification endpoint (results cached in Redis).
      POSTA_EMAIL_VERIFY_ENABLED: "true"
      POSTA_EMAIL_VERIFY_CACHE_TTL_HOURS: "168"
      POSTA_EMAIL_VERIFY_MX_CACHE_TTL_HOURS: "24"
      POSTA_EMAIL_VERIFY_RATE_HOURLY: "1000"
    secretEnv:
      - POSTA_ADMIN_PASSWORD
    healthcheck:
      type: http
      path: /healthz
      port: 9000
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 10

  # Background processing: email delivery, retries of failed messages, and
  # scheduled tasks. Same image, started with the `worker` command, so it scales
  # independently of the API.
  - name: worker
    image: jkaninda/posta
    tag: "0.13.1"
    command: ["worker"]
    env:
      POSTA_WORKER_CONCURRENCY: "10"
      POSTA_WORKER_MAX_RETRIES: "5"
    healthcheck:
      # No listener to probe — the worker's liveness is the queue draining.
      type: none

apiVersion: miabi.io/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: valkey
  displayName: Valkey
  version: 1.0.0
  description: High-performance key-value store and cache — the community fork of Redis.
  category: Database
  icon: https://github.com/valkey-io.png
  homepage: https://valkey.io
  tags: [database, cache, key-value, redis]
inputs:
  - key: password
    label: Password
    help: "Password clients must authenticate with (requirepass). Leave blank to auto-generate. Letters, digits and - _ . : @ only, no spaces."
    type: password
    generate: true
    length: 24
    required: true
    pattern: '^[A-Za-z0-9._:@-]{8,}$'
volumes:
  - name: data
applications:
  - name: valkey
    primary: true
    image: valkey/valkey
    tag: "9-alpine"
    # The image entrypoint appends $VALKEY_EXTRA_FLAGS to the default
    # `valkey-server` command, so auth and persistence are set without overriding
    # the command — which would skip the entrypoint's drop-to-valkey-user step.
    env:
      VALKEY_PASSWORD: "{{ .inputs.password }}"
      VALKEY_EXTRA_FLAGS: "--requirepass {{ .inputs.password }} --appendonly yes"
    secretEnv:
      - VALKEY_PASSWORD
      - VALKEY_EXTRA_FLAGS
    mounts:
      - volume: data
        path: /data
    healthcheck:
      type: command
      command: valkey-cli -a "$VALKEY_PASSWORD" --no-auth-warning ping | grep -q PONG
      intervalSeconds: 30
      timeoutSeconds: 5
      retries: 3
      startPeriodSeconds: 10
